category: PCB Editor board setup, placement, constraints & routing
description: Setting up an OrCAD PCB Editor / Presto board and getting it placed and routed: board creation and stackup, importing the logic from Capture, placement aids, the Constraint Manager and its physical, spacing, electrical, differential-pair and matched-group rules, interactive and automatic routing, copper shapes and planes, and design rule checking.

tools.name: New Board / Board Wizard
tools.description: Creates a board database. The Board Wizard walks through units and drawing size, the design template to inherit defaults from, the layer count and stackup, default spacing constraints, default via padstack and an optional rectangular or circular board outline, producing a ready-to-place .brd. Use it instead of starting from a blank drawing so that units, grids and DRC defaults are coherent.
tools.usage: File > New > Board (wizard), or File > New > Drawing type 'Board (wizard)'

parameters.name: Units / Drawing size
parameters.description: Mils, inches, millimetres or microns and the sheet extents; changing units later is possible but disruptive.

parameters.name: Template
parameters.description: A .brd or .dra to inherit colours, grids, subclasses and default constraints from.

parameters.name: Etch layer count
parameters.description: Number of routing layers; the stackup is refined afterwards in the Cross-Section Editor.

parameters.name: Default spacing constraints
parameters.description: Line-to-line, line-to-pad and pad-to-pad clearances used to seed the default constraint set.

tools.example: File > New > Board (wizard) > Units: mils, size B > 4 etch layers > default spacing 8 mils > rectangular outline 4000 x 3000 mils.
tools.notes: In OrCAD X Presto the equivalent flow is driven from the Design Setup panel rather than a modal wizard.

tools.name: Cross-Section Editor (layer stackup)
tools.description: Defines the physical stackup: the ordered list of conductor, dielectric and plane layers with thickness, material, dielectric constant, loss tangent and copper weight, plus negative/positive artwork and which layers are plane layers. The impedance column computes a trace's characteristic impedance from the geometry, so the stackup is also where controlled-impedance targets are validated.
tools.usage: Setup > Cross-section… (also reachable from the Constraint Manager)

parameters.name: Layer Type
parameters.description: Conductor, Plane or Dielectric.

parameters.name: Thickness / Material
parameters.description: Per-layer physical thickness and material, driving impedance and total board thickness.

parameters.name: Negative Artwork
parameters.description: Marks a plane layer to be plotted as a negative, which is normal for solid planes.

parameters.name: Dielectric Constant / Loss Tangent
parameters.description: Feeds impedance calculation and signal-integrity extraction.

tools.example: Setup > Cross-section > insert two internal plane layers, set core thickness 0.2 mm Er 4.3, prepreg 0.1 mm, then read the impedance column for a 0.15 mm microstrip.
tools.notes: Adding or reordering layers after routing exists forces a re-check of every via span; do stackup work before serious routing.

tools.name: Design Parameters (Setup > Design Parameters)
tools.description: The global preferences of the board: units and accuracy, drawing extents, display options (filled pads, connect-line style, rat display), text block table, shape fill behaviour, and route keep-out enforcement. Several later frustrations (shapes not filling, text too small, DRCs not showing) are settings on these tabs.
tools.usage: Setup > Design Parameters… (tabs: Display, Design, Text, Shapes, Flow Planning, Route)
tools.example: Setup > Design Parameters > Display > tick 'Filled pads' and 'Connect line' > Shapes tab > set the default dynamic fill to Smooth.

tools.name: Import Logic / Netrev
tools.description: Loads the logical design from Capture into the board. It reads the three pst*.dat files that Capture's PCB Editor netlister produced (pstchip.dat, pstxnet.dat, pstxprt.dat), creates or updates components, nets and ratsnest connections, and reports differences. On re-import it behaves as an incremental ECO, preserving existing placement and routing.
tools.usage: File > Import > Logic… > Cadence tab > point at the netlist directory > Import Cadence

parameters.name: Import directory
parameters.description: Folder holding pstchip.dat, pstxnet.dat and pstxprt.dat.

parameters.name: Place changed component
parameters.description: Always / If same symbol / Never — controls whether a changed part is re-placed or kept.

parameters.name: Ignore FIXED property
parameters.description: Allows the import to move components that are marked fixed.

parameters.name: Create user-defined properties / Create PCB parts
parameters.description: Carries Capture properties into the board database.

tools.example: File > Import > Logic > Cadence > Import directory 'allegro' > Place changed component: If same symbol > Import Cadence; check netrev.lst for unresolved footprints.
tools.notes: Every component must have a PCB Footprint property that resolves to a .psm on the library path; unresolved symbols are listed in netrev.lst and are the most common import failure.

tools.name: Quickplace
tools.description: Bulk-places all unplaced components automatically outside or inside the board outline, grouped by schematic page, net, room, part type or property value. It is a starting arrangement, not a placement solution, but it replaces hours of dragging parts out of the bin before manual placement begins.
tools.usage: Place > Quickplace…

parameters.name: Placement Filter
parameters.description: Place by property/value, room, part number, net name or schematic page number.

parameters.name: Place by
parameters.description: Around the board outline, inside it, or by partition.

parameters.name: Unplaced symbol count
parameters.description: Live feedback on what remains to place.

tools.example: Place > Quickplace > Placement filter: Place by schematic page number > page 2 > Place > components from page 2 appear grouped beside the outline.

tools.name: Place Manual
tools.description: The interactive placement dialog: a browsable list of unplaced components (and mechanical symbols, format symbols and package symbols) that attaches the selected item to the cursor. Options control mirroring, rotation, the placement grid and whether the ratsnest is shown while dragging, so a part can be positioned against its connectivity.
tools.usage: Place > Manually… (Place > Component Manually in some builds)
tools.example: Place > Manually > Components by refdes > tick U3 > click the target location > right-click > Done.
tools.notes: Hold the right mouse button for Rotate/Mirror/Snap-to options while the part is on the cursor.

tools.name: Place Replicate
tools.description: Captures the placement and routing of one instance of a repeated circuit and applies it to the other instances, matching components by their hierarchical relationship. For a board with eight identical channels it turns a day of work into minutes and guarantees the channels are electrically identical.
tools.usage: Place > Replicate Create… (capture a module), then Place > Replicate Apply…
tools.example: Place > Replicate Create > select channel A's components and traces > save module 'chanA.mdd'; Place > Replicate Apply > pick channel B's anchor component > the placement and routing are mirrored across.

tools.name: Rooms
tools.description: Named regions of the board that components can be assigned to, so that a functional block is constrained to an area. Rooms are drawn on the Room subclass, assigned to components as a ROOM property (often forward-annotated from the schematic), and enforced by the Placement constraints in the Constraint Manager.
tools.usage: Setup > Outlines > Room Outline…; assign with Edit > Properties > ROOM, or via the Constraint Manager
tools.example: Setup > Outlines > Room Outline > draw 'PSU' over the power section; assign ROOM=PSU to the regulator components; Quickplace by room then drops them inside it.

tools.name: Add Connect (interactive routing)
tools.description: The primary routing command. Click a pin, via or trace end and route interactively; the Options panel selects the active and alternate layers, line width and via padstack, and right-click offers Add Via, Change Layer, Finish, Snap to connect point and Neck Mode. Online DRC enforces the constraint set as the trace is drawn.
tools.usage: Route > Connect (Add Connect); Options panel sets Act/Alt layer, Line width, Via

parameters.name: Act / Alt layer
parameters.description: Active routing layer and the layer a via change switches to.

parameters.name: Line width
parameters.description: Width for new segments, defaulting to the net's Physical constraint.

parameters.name: Line lock
parameters.description: Line/Arc and 45/90/Off angle locking.

parameters.name: Bubble / Shove preferred
parameters.description: Whether existing traces are pushed aside or the new trace hugs them.

tools.example: Route > Connect, click U1 pin 14, set Line width 8, click to route, press the right button > Add Via to change layer, double-click on the destination pad to finish.
tools.notes: Bubble 'Shove preferred' plus 'Smooth' gives the closest behaviour to a modern push-and-shove router.

tools.name: Slide
tools.description: Drags an existing trace segment, corner or via while maintaining connectivity and pushing or hugging neighbouring traces according to the bubble setting. It is how routing is tidied and how room is made for a new trace without ripping anything up.
tools.usage: Route > Slide (or Edit > Slide); pick a segment or corner and drag
tools.example: Route > Slide, grab the middle segment of the clock trace and drag it 20 mils away from the switching node; neighbouring traces shove aside.

tools.name: Delete / Unroute (Ripup)
tools.description: Removes routing. Edit > Delete with the Find Filter set to Clines removes selected segments; Route > Unroute > Net/Component/Selection converts routed connections back to ratsnest lines. Ripping up a net is the normal first step when re-routing a signal that has been shoved into a bad shape.
tools.usage: Edit > Delete with Find Filter Cline/Cline Segs; Route > Unroute > Net | Component
tools.example: Set the Find Filter to Nets, Route > Unroute > Net, click DDR_CK — the whole net returns to ratsnest.

tools.name: Auto-interactive routing (AiDT / Auto Route)
tools.description: Semi-automatic routing where the designer defines the start, end and general path and the tool completes the connection legally, adding vias and obeying constraints; the fuller Route > Route Automatic engine routes selected nets, components or the whole board unattended with strategy passes (fanout, route, clean-up, via minimisation). Use auto-interactive for hard signals and full autoroute only for low-speed fill-in.
tools.usage: Route > Route Automatic… ; Route > Auto-interactive Delay/Phase Tune; Route > Fanout

parameters.name: Selection scope
parameters.description: Whole design, selected nets, selected components or a window.

parameters.name: Strategy / Passes
parameters.description: Fanout, routing, clean-up and via-reduction passes with pass counts.

parameters.name: Protect existing routes
parameters.description: Prevents the engine from ripping up manual work.

tools.example: Route > Route Automatic > Selection: 'Route selected nets' > tick 'Protect existing routes' > Route.
tools.notes: Autorouting ignores nothing that is in the constraint set — if the result looks wrong, the constraints are usually wrong.

tools.name: Constraint Manager
tools.description: The spreadsheet that owns every design rule, shared between Capture and the board. Worksheets are grouped into Electrical (signal integrity, propagation delay, relative delay, differential pairs, impedance, wiring/vias, return path), Physical (line width, via list, neck width, allowed layers), Spacing (all the object-to-object clearances), Same Net Spacing, Properties and Manufacturing (DFM/DFA). Rules are organised into constraint sets applied to design, layer, class, net class, net, xnet, bus, differential pair or pin pair, with the most specific winning.
tools.usage: Setup > Constraints > Constraint Manager… (or the CM toolbar button)

parameters.name: Physical CSet
parameters.description: Line width min/max, neck width and length, via list, allowed etch layers.

parameters.name: Spacing CSet
parameters.description: Line-to-line/pad/via/shape, pad-to-pad, via-to-via, hole-to-hole and bond-finger clearances.

parameters.name: Electrical CSet
parameters.description: Max propagation delay, relative delay/matched groups, impedance, differential pair coupling and uncoupled length, max via count, return path.

parameters.name: Region
parameters.description: Constraint region shapes that apply a different CSet inside a board area, e.g. tighter rules under a BGA.

tools.example: Constraint Manager > Physical > Net > All Layers > create CSet 'POWER' with Min Line Width 20 mil; assign the VBUS and GND nets to it; the online DRC now enforces 20 mil.
tools.notes: Constraints entered in Capture (OrCAD X) appear here automatically; editing them on the board and not syncing back is a common source of schematic/board divergence.

tools.name: Net classes and class-class rules
tools.description: Groups of nets that share constraints — for example DDR_ADDR, POWER, ANALOG. Assigning a Physical or Spacing constraint set to a class covers every member net at once, and class-to-class spacing rules set the clearance between two groups (e.g. 40 mil between ANALOG and SWITCHING) without touching the per-net rules.
tools.usage: Constraint Manager > Objects/Net > create Net Class, drag nets in; Spacing > Class-Class worksheet for inter-class clearance
tools.example: Create net classes PRIMARY and SECONDARY, then in Spacing > Class-Class set PRIMARY-SECONDARY clearance to 8 mm for creepage on an isolated supply.

tools.name: Differential pairs
tools.description: Declares two nets as a pair so the router treats them as one object: primary gap, primary width, neck gap and width, maximum uncoupled length and phase (intra-pair skew) tolerance are set in the Constraint Manager, and Route > Connect then routes both members together. Pairs can be created automatically by name pattern (_P/_N, +/-) or manually.
tools.usage: Constraint Manager > Electrical > Net > Routing > Differential Pair; create pairs manually or with Auto Generate

parameters.name: Primary Gap / Primary Width
parameters.description: Target edge-to-edge spacing and trace width for the coupled section.

parameters.name: (-)Tolerance / (+)Tolerance
parameters.description: Allowed deviation before a DRC is raised.

parameters.name: Max Uncoupled Length
parameters.description: How far the pair may separate, e.g. at a breakout.

parameters.name: Phase Tolerance
parameters.description: Permitted intra-pair length mismatch, tuned out with Auto-interactive Phase Tune.

tools.example: Auto Generate pairs by the `_P/_N` filter, set Primary Gap 5 mil / Width 5 mil / Max Uncoupled 500 mil, then route USB_D with Route > Connect — both traces follow the cursor.

tools.name: Matched groups / relative propagation delay
tools.description: Length- or delay-matching across a set of nets, used for memory byte lanes and source-synchronous buses. A match group with a target and tolerance is created in the Electrical worksheet; the Constraint Manager then reports each member's actual versus required delay in real time, and Route > Auto-interactive Delay Tune adds serpentine to close the gap.
tools.usage: Constraint Manager > Electrical > Net > Routing > Relative Propagation Delay; create a Match Group with Delta:Tolerance
tools.example: Create match group DQ0_BYTE with target net DQS0, tolerance ±25 mil; route the byte lane, then Route > Auto-interactive Delay Tune on each short net until the worksheet turns green.

tools.name: Shape Add (copper pours)
tools.description: Creates copper areas: dynamic shapes automatically void around pins, vias, traces and other shapes and re-flow whenever the design changes, while static shapes are fixed geometry that must be manually updated. Assign the shape to a net so that thermal reliefs and connections are generated according to the padstack's thermal definitions.
tools.usage: Shape > Polygon | Rectangular | Circular; Options panel sets Active layer, Net assignment and Shape Fill type (Dynamic copper / Static solid / Unfilled)

parameters.name: Shape Fill Type
parameters.description: Dynamic copper (auto-voiding, the normal choice), Static solid, Static crosshatch or Unfilled.

parameters.name: Assign net name
parameters.description: Net the pour connects to; unassigned shapes are floating copper.

parameters.name: Dynamic fill
parameters.description: Smooth (full recompute), Rough (approximate while editing) or Disabled (defer until Shape > Global Dynamic Params > Update).

tools.example: Shape > Rectangular > Active layer BOTTOM, Net GND, Dynamic copper > draw over the board area > the pour voids automatically around every via and trace.
tools.notes: Set Shape > Global Dynamic Params > Dynamic fill to 'Rough' while routing heavily, then back to 'Smooth' and Update to Smooth before generating artwork.

tools.name: Shape editing (void, boundary, island removal)
tools.description: Maintenance commands for pours: Shape > Manual Void carves a hole (rectangle, polygon, circle or around an element), Shape > Edit Boundary reshapes an existing pour, Shape > Delete Islands removes disconnected copper fragments, Shape > Merge Shapes combines overlapping same-net shapes, and Shape > Check checks for slivers and unconnected islands.
tools.usage: Shape > Manual Void > Polygon | Rectangular | Circular | Element; Shape > Edit Boundary; Shape > Delete Islands; Shape > Merge Shapes
tools.example: Shape > Delete Islands > All > the isolated GND fragments under the connector disappear and the DRC count drops.

tools.name: Plane layers and split planes
tools.description: Internal plane layers are defined in the Cross-Section Editor and are normally plotted as negatives. A solid plane is drawn as a dynamic shape on the plane layer; splitting it into multiple voltage islands is done by drawing several net-assigned shapes on the same layer with the anti-etch between them, giving separate 3V3, 1V8 and VCORE regions on one layer.
tools.usage: Setup > Cross-section > set Layer Type Plane; then Shape > Polygon per voltage island with the appropriate net
tools.example: On layer IN2 draw one shape for 3V3 covering the digital section and a second for 1V8 under the core, leaving 20 mil of anti-etch between them.
tools.notes: Check for splits crossed by high-speed signals: the Constraint Manager's Return Path checks flag traces whose reference plane is discontinuous.

tools.name: Design Rule Check (DRC)
tools.description: Verifies the layout against the constraint set. Online DRC checks continuously as you edit; Tools > Update DRC re-checks the whole design (or just the out-of-date regions). Violations become DRC markers on the board and rows in the DRC browser, from which each can be selected and cross-probed. A board is not ready for manufacture until the DRC count is zero or every remaining marker is a reviewed waiver.
tools.usage: Setup > Constraints > Modes (enable online checks); Tools > Update DRC…; Display > Status for the current counts

parameters.name: Update all / Update out-of-date
parameters.description: Full recheck versus incremental recheck of changed areas.

parameters.name: DRC modes
parameters.description: Per-check on/off switches for the many geometric, same-net and manufacturing checks.

parameters.name: Waived DRCs
parameters.description: Markers explicitly accepted by the designer, reported separately from live errors.

tools.example: Tools > Update DRC > Update all > Display > Status shows 0 DRC errors, 0 unrouted, 3 waived.
tools.notes: Display > Status is the fastest health check of a board: it shows unrouted connections, DRC errors, out-of-date shapes and unplaced parts in one panel.

tools.name: Fanout
tools.description: Automatically adds an escape trace and via for every pin of selected components — the standard preparation for BGAs and dense SMD parts before routing begins. Options control via placement pattern, whether vias go inside or outside the footprint, whether SMD pins are fanned to planes, and via sharing between pins of the same net.
tools.usage: Route > Fanout… (Route > Create Fanout)
tools.example: Select U7 (a 256-ball BGA), Route > Fanout, pattern 'Via in centre of 4 pads', tick 'Share vias on same net', Fanout — every ball now has a via to an inner layer.

tools.name: Test points
tools.description: Creates and manages in-circuit-test access: automatic test point generation places a test point (via, pad or on an existing pad) on each net subject to grid, layer, clearance and one-per-net rules, and the test point report plus the IPC-D-356 netlist feed the fixture. Rules are set under Setup > Constraints and the commands under Manufacture > Testprep.
tools.usage: Manufacture > Testprep > Automatic…, Manual…, Parameters…, Report…

parameters.name: Test point pad/via
parameters.description: Which padstack a generated test point uses.

parameters.name: Grid
parameters.description: Probe grid the test points must snap to (e.g. 100 mil for a bed-of-nails fixture).

parameters.name: Allow test point on component pins/vias
parameters.description: Whether existing features may be re-used instead of adding new ones.

tools.example: Manufacture > Testprep > Parameters (grid 100 mil, bottom side only) > Automatic > Generate testpoints; then Manufacture > Testprep > Report for the coverage summary.

tools.name: Display > Status and Display > Element
tools.description: The two everyday inspection commands. Display > Status summarises the board's health — unrouted connections, DRC errors, waived DRCs, out-of-date shapes, unplaced components — in one panel with buttons to update each. Display > Element reports everything the database knows about a clicked object: net, layer, width, padstack, length, constraints in force.
tools.usage: Display > Status…; Display > Element then click an object
tools.example: Display > Status > shows 12 unrouted, 0 DRC, 2 out-of-date shapes > click Update to re-flow the shapes.
tools.notes: Out-of-date shapes must be updated before artwork generation or the plotted copper will not match what is on screen.

tools.name: Constraint Manager (from Capture)
tools.description: Opens the shared Allegro Constraint Manager on the schematic so that electrical constraints — net classes, differential pairs, matched groups, relative and absolute propagation delay, impedance — are authored in Capture and travel with the design into the board. Front-end constraints entered here appear automatically in PCB Editor and drive online DRC during routing.
tools.usage: PCB > Constraint Manager (OrCAD X Capture, requires a licence that includes Constraint Manager)
tools.example: PCB > Constraint Manager > Electrical > Net > Routing > Differential Pair, create pair USB_DP/USB_DN, set the target impedance and coupling tolerance.
tools.notes: Not available in the base OrCAD Capture-only licence; it comes with the OrCAD X Professional/Allegro tiers.
